newsitem.title: USA: Copper prices set 5-month high, natural gas.
newsitem.headline: Copper prices set 5-month high, natural gas.

text.p: Copper futures prices set a five-month high Tuesday in New York markets following a similar rise in London keyed to tight supplies.
Natural gas futures rose on the New York Mercantile Exchange as frigid air due later this week across the United States should keep furnaces lit and further tax already low gas stocks.
Cocoa jumped to six-week highs Tuesday largely on speculative shortcovering prompted by gains in London.

In copper, a drop in London stockpiles triggered buying first in London markets and later in New York's Commodity Exchange (COMEX) copper futures. The London Metal Exchange reported copper registered for delivery against exchange contracts fell to 90,050 metric tons this past week, the lowest in six years.
"Falling stocks and rising demand could result in a severe physical squeeze in the next three to six months," said a report from the London brokerage firm Bain and Co.
Further, Bain forcasts demand will outpace world copper supplies by 100,000 to 200,000 tons in 1996.
In the United States, copper prices seasonally move higher in the fourth quarter as demand for copper building materials rises ahead of the spring and summer home building season.

"Part of it (the price increase) is a seasonal upturn in demand," said David Rinehimer, Smith Barney's director of futures research. "(Also) There has been speculation the Chinese may be building inventories."
COMEX copper for December delivery closed up 2.30 cents at 108.20 cents per lb., but peaked Tuesday at 109.90 the highest since mid-June.
Natural gas prices sped higher as a second storm system was forming in the southern United States and may spread snow and frigid cold from Texas to the eastern seaboard.
The central and eastern parts of the United States continued to dig out Tuesday from a storm that spread ice and snow from Texas up the Atlantic coast, caused 19 deaths and knocked out power.
In addition to increased heating use, New York traders and analysts said natural gas supplies are low.
Total U.S. gas inventories were 6 percent less than a year ago at 181 billion cubic feet, according to the American Gas Association weekly storage report released last Wednesday.

NYMEX January natural gas futures were up 8.7 cents Tuesday at $3.581 per million British thermal units, off from the contract high of $3.68 set Friday. The $3.68 is the second highest price since December 1995, trailing only the volatile close Thursday when the expiring December contract hit $4.05.

In other NYMEX energy markets, lower cash markets weighed on heating oil futures with December off 0.99 cent at 71.24 cents per gallon. Gasoline futures followed cash higher with December up 1.02 cents at 69.01 cents per gallon and crude oil rose with gasoline with January up 13 cents at $23.62 per barrel.
Cocoa futures moved higher, propelled by technical shortcovering, motivated by gains in London markets and by a Commodity Futures Trading Commission report showing large short positions.

Prudential Securities analyst Arthur Stevenson said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data, which showed a net speculative short position of 2,782 lots in the two weeks ended Nov. 19, made the market vunerable to a shortcovering rally.
March cocoa ended $27 higher at $1,416 a metric ton, its highest level since Oct. 18. December ended up $30, to $1,371.
Additionally, traders said reports that the Ivorian crop could be adversely affected by prolonged dry weather during the tail end of the current main crop provided underlying support to the market.
